fixes.explanation: Quiet would have been the safe play, friend. But the text says they cried out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (Matthew 20:30). I went quiet for a while in the back of a junk drawer, and all I got was dust. These two chose the opposite.

Good thinking, but the text never says they moved at all. They were sitting beside the road, and when they heard Jesus was passing by, they cried out (Matthew 20:30). What the text shows them using is their voices, aimed straight at Him.

Right, baker. Matthew says, "The crowd admonished them to be silent…" (Matthew 20:31). That's a whole crowd telling two men to pipe down. Imagine trying to shout your order at a counter while the whole line goes "shhhh."
Nice guess, but tomorrow never comes up. The text says the crowd admonished them to be silent (Matthew 20:31). That's the instruction the crowd gives.
The text says nothing about them walking away, baker. It says they "cried out all the louder, 'Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!'" (Matthew 20:31). Louder is the direction they went.

Yes, baker. "Jesus stopped and called them." (Matthew 20:32). A large crowd was following Him as He left Jericho (Matthew 20:29), and He stopped for two men sitting by the road. I think that tells you plenty about who gets His attention.
Not here, friend. Matthew says, "Jesus stopped and called them." (Matthew 20:32). He didn't keep walking past. These two had heard that He was passing by, and He stopped.
That was the crowd's move, baker, not His. The crowd admonished them to be silent (Matthew 20:31). But Jesus "…stopped and called them." (Matthew 20:32). The text doesn't describe anyone being sent.
Good guess, friend, but ears aren't what they asked about. They heard that Jesus was passing by (Matthew 20:30). What they asked for was, "let our eyes be opened." (Matthew 20:33).
